newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-KULIK AND ZAGORODNIUK BACK TO THEIR BEST.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-KULIK AND ZAGORODNIUK BACK TO THEIR BEST.

text.p: Russian Ilya Kulik and Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine put poor qualifying displays behind them to dominate the men's short programme at the European figure skating championships on Wednesday.
Kulik, champion in 1995, and Zagorodniuk, champion last year, called on their experience to snatch the top two places after skating far below their best in qualifying on Sunday.

Fourth and sixth in their qualifying group, both skaters performed the key element of the short programme -- the jump combination -- superbly, each completing a difficult triple axel linked with a triple toe loop.

"Sunday was worrying because I was trying to do my best but on another level I wasn't worried because I know I've been skating well," said Kulik, winner of the title at 17 on his senior debut two years ago.
Zagorodniuk appeared near-perfect but felt he had made some minor errors. He was satisfied, however, with his triple-triple, the vital move which ruined the chances of other skaters.
Andrei Vlascenko, a former Latvian who now skates for Germany, produced a surprise by taking third place with French favourite Philippe Candeloro fourth.
Vlascenko produced a triple-axel-triple toe loop for the first time but would not admit to being surprised by his result.
"I'm just happy with my place and happy with what I did," said Vlascenko.
Candeloro fluffed his short programmes in last year's European and world championships, finishing fifth and ninth respectively, and was determined to do better in front of his home fans.
He also achieved the triple-triple but had a minor l problem with the subsequent triple lutz, which he has trouble with because of a foot injury.
"I felt under pressure but I'm glad to be fourth and now I want to be in the top three," he said.
The men's medals will be decided in the free skating on Thursday night.
Russians Alexei Yagudin and Olympic champion Alexei Urmanov, who missed his combination, held fifth and sixth places followed by Ukrainians Evgeny Pliuta and former champion Dmitry Dmitrenko.
Azerbaijani Igor Pashkevitch, second last year skating for Russia, also missed the combination, falling on the first jump. He was ninth on Wednesday.
Briton Steven Cousins, fourth last year, managed only 10th place, six positions ahead of new British champion Neil Wilson.
Cousins briefly lost control landing his triple axel in combination and just managed the second jump, a double toe loop."It was a minor error but it was enough to get killed. That's life," he said.
